title: SGEMM from scratch
brief: Write fp32 matrix-multiplication kernels in CUDA C++, from a naive one-thread-per-output kernel to a shared-memory tiled kernel and a 2D register-blocked kernel, and measure each as a percentage of cuBLAS.
hints: Compiling the CUDA source takes 30 to 60 seconds the first time. Later runs reuse the cache.
Start with the pure-Python helpers: FLOPs are 2*M*N*K, and the least traffic is 4 bytes times (M*K + K*N + M*N).
In the tiled kernel, every thread must reach both __syncthreads() calls, so guard the loads and the final store, never the whole loop body. Load 0.0 for an element outside the matrix.
In the register-blocked kernel, store A's tile transposed, As[k * BM + m], so a thread's TM values for one k are contiguous in shared memory.
Each k step of the register-blocked kernel is an outer product: read TM values of A and TN values of B into registers, then do TM*TN FMAs.
To add the optional kernels, define sgemm_coalesced and sgemm_vectorized, then add their names to FUNCTIONS and their signatures to CPP_DECLARATIONS. The tests measure whatever FUNCTIONS lists.
float4 loads need K % 4 == 0, N % 4 == 0, and 16-byte aligned pointers. Fall back to scalar loads when that is false, or the odd-size tests fail.
